I've been farming this same land in Quzhou for fifty years. I know what works. My children have gone to the city to work, so it is mostly me and my wife managing the fields now. At my age I cannot do heavy work all day, but I know this soil and I know this system.

**My thinking:**

The 3 mu will all go through wheat first, then maize — same as every year. I plant wheat in October and harvest in June, then turn around and put maize in right away. No point splitting the land differently; the rotation works and the soil knows it.

For wheat, I will use the improved variety the seed cooperative has been selling for years — I have used it for at least a decade and it performs well here. I will rotary-till after the maize harvest in September, then apply compound fertilizer (二铵) and urea as base, then top-dress urea again in spring when the wheat greens up. I water three times: winter water before the ground freezes, jointing water in April, and one more around heading. I will spray herbicide once in autumn and maybe a fungicide pass in late spring if the weather is wet. I expect around 450 kg per mu — that is what I normally get.

For maize, I direct-seed right after wheat harvest in June — no point tilling in the summer heat. I buy hybrid seed, same brand I used last few years. I put compound fertilizer in the furrow at planting, then chase it with urea at the big bell stage. Summer gets rain so I usually only need to pump well water once, maybe during pollination if it is dry. Corn borer has been a problem some years so I spray for that, plus herbicide at emergence. I expect around 550 kg per mu.

I am not going to experiment this year. I am 71. These methods feed my family and give me some income. That is enough.
